utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. A very good morning to everybody. May we hear the case number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, with Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic, John Ostojic, and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we have Mr. Pusac as our witness today. I hope you had a nice evening in The Hague yesterday, and time to think about what we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And let me go --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- in medias res, in the -- following the last question of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may please the witness be shown once again from S180, item 97. This is in the English version, page 69. And at the same time, D50B. This is the sketch drawn by the witness. Questioned by the Court: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Pusac, yesterday I asked you for some assistance for a better understanding of this conclusion of 29 May 1992. What does it mean? "Because of the formation of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the need for the Serbian Territorial Defence has ceased." Why this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert who could give you response on the meaning, on the legal meaning of this conclusion, but in the army - that is, in my command as a soldier, as a medical officer and a doctor - I don't remember ever having received an order regarding this issue or an explanation as to why the Territorial Defence has ceased to exist and what is the meaning of that. That is why now and here, relying on my medical knowledge, my professional knowledge, I cannot answer your question because I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then turn to the second sentence of this conclusion that is even closer to your own sketch. "The Serbian Territorial Defence shall be incorporated into the structure of the region and placed under its command." So as I asked you already yesterday, where in your own sketch, Exhibit D50B, would you allocate now the Serbian Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, the Serbian Territorial Defence did not exist, as far as I know. And I, as a doctor, did not have any contacts with the bodies of the Territorial Defence. So I can't tell you precisely which box would contain the Territorial Defence. If you will allow me, Your Honour, I would like to once again clarify this position of mine. So if you want me to do that, I will gladly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we all did understand this, but maybe from a more practical point of view, have you ever been involved in assistance - medical care, medical assistance - given to members of the Serbian Territorial Defence, be it before the war or during the war?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, during the peacetimes, I've already told you that the Territorial Defence was a well-known term and a well-known institution. When we had military drills, I did have an opportunity to treat people, but I don't remember having registered them as members of the Territorial Defence. All these people were just patients for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. That's the spirit a physician should work in no doubt. But what about wartime, during wartime? Has anything changed?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, I was a physician, and I was surrounded by the wounded, by the sick, by the civilian casualties or participants in the war, but I don't remember -- I can't remember anybody wearing the insignia of the Territorial Defence with whom I would have personal contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this insignia would be?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know what insignia would it be, because as far as I know, even before the war there were no particular insignia on their uniforms or some other form of recognition of members of the Territorial Defence. At least, I didn't know of any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that you made no distinction related to your patients, and you weren't aware at all whether your patient was now a member of the regular army or the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever came to me and was wounded or sick was given assistance regardless of whether he was a fighter or a civilian, whether he was a Muslim or a Serb. They were all treated equally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were there also Muslims in the Serbian Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of this institution, of that category. So I'm not in a position to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the moment, I myself don't have any further questions. Judge Vassylenko, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I have several questions. Mr. Pusac, was the Minister of Defence in the former Yugoslavia a member of the Yugoslavian government?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was the Minister of Defence bound by the decisions adopted by the highest political leadership of the country?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not engage in politics. I could partly answer your question as regards the military chain of command. So the Supreme Command and the subordinate parts, that is what I know. But as for the politics, I never engaged in any politics, and that's why I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Who decided on the formation of the armed forces of Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Radovan Karadzic and his political aides or General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer this question with any degree of precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Now I have some questions related to the Exhibit S346 containing the order of General Talic on general mobilisation. Doctor, may I ask you to read out paragraph 8 of this document. It's page 3 of the B/C/S version. The first line of this paragraph and then subparagraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 8 is on page 2 in my version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Page 2, yes. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Until the units receive concrete combat tasks, engage them in the following tasks: Maintain and improve the operational and tactical positions of own units, increase the military and combat compactness of wartime units, conduct intensive combat training, focusing on firing and tactical training, and establish the closest possible cooperation with the people and legal authorities within their zones of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask the Defence team and the interpreters to help me to translate the words "legalnim organima."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Legal bodies."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: "Legal," not "legitimate"?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May the Court please repeat the word? We don't have it in front of us in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, in subparagraph 4, we have the expression "legalnim organima."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it can mean both "legitimate" and "legal." I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: It's sooner"legitimate."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters agree with Counsel Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In legitimate and legal. Now, Mr. Pusac, on the first page of the document, it is said that general work duty has been introduced. Can you explain us what is "general work duty"?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert, but as a layperson, based on what was happening, I can give you my assessment as to what that may have been. It's a form of obligation according to which the employees would turn to work and maybe stay longer because of the needs imposed by the war. And in that sense, they had a higher degree of obligation than during the time of peace, but I'm not an expert, and I cannot give you a precise definition of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was the work duty introduced as in relation to your position, to yourself?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the medical battalion, and obviously, as far as I can remember, there was this duty imposed on the majority of institutions, and I believe that this was also the case in health care institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In this document, in the order signed by General Talic is the reference to the mobilisation of the SZ, Civilian Protection. On the first page, in the preamble of the document.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understood it in the following way: The civilian population is being mobilised. Mobilisation is under way. The Civilian Protection is being mobilised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And can you explain me what is the difference between Civilian Protection and Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the Civilian Protection are peacetime units intended primarily to act in a natural disaster, such as earthquakes, floods of greater proportions. That is when they are engaged to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Then why the mobilisation of Civilian Protection was announced and was under way at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the Presidency of Republika Srpska, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina came to the conclusion that the Civilian Protection had to be mobilised. I don't know. My command was not in charge of making these decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Well, I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Argibay, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Doctor. I would like to ask you if you knew at the time of the takeover of power that occurred in Prijedor on April 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard that there had been a shake-up or a change among the elected and appointed officials. I heard that a different political option or party had arrived. But I was in the army in Banja Luka, and I really didn't have much information that would give me more insight into that event, which was the takeover of power in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Would you say that the military was involved in that takeover?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such information, nor did anybody in my command inform me about that or order me to participate or to learn more details on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Would you think it likely that the military were involved with that takeover?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, because this was a political issue. Otherwise, it would have been a local military coup. What I'm trying to say is that the army was not a municipal or a regional institution. It belonged to the entire republic. So neither a municipal body or a regional body could command the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is another question: Have you heard about the camp collection centres or investigation centres that were in Prijedor in 1992, between May and, say, August, September, something like that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that information, but since I was in Banja Luka in the command only at the beginning of these events and then I was absent for a few months due to my illness, I had to spend some time in Belgrade, so I don't have any details on these. I don't have any information to be able to tell you more. The only thing I could tell you is what I heard from the -- from the media or what I heard from my parents once I returned from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: So you're not aware that the military had anything to do with those camps?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have that information. I have never seen a document which would corroborate the fact that the army did this or that. I simply don't have such information or such material evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Due to the -- this schedule you made yourself, the document that's now D50B - you have it, I think, there - is it not the president of the republic, I don't know with the consent of the parliament or not, that's another problem, but the president of the republic, the one who is in charge of declaring war or signing peace treaties?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I don't know that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Who do you suppose declares war and mobilises the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose, based on my knowledge, that it will be the Supreme Commander or the president of the state, or maybe it is the parliament. I do not have so much political knowledge to be able to give you the exact information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: So the Supreme Commander, that's the president of the state; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have no doubt that the Defence has another line of questions. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have quite a few questions emanating from yours and questions from my learned friends. Re-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, good morning, Dr. Pusac. I told you that your testimony shouldn't take long, but it seems I wasn't right in saying that. The reason is that all of us here are trying to use you as an expert on constitutional law. So in keeping with that line of questioning, you will have to muster additional strength and answer a couple of questions of mine, mostly in connection with constitutional law, if you can answer them. If not, you are free to say that you can't answer because you don't know the answer. I have handed in a list of documents to the registry, and I would kindly ask for the usher to receive the set. Let's start with the document D3. [In English] It's a statute. [Interpretation] Doctor, would you please take the statute. This is just a working copy. We don't have a better version. This is the statute of Prijedor municipality. Can you open it on page 12. It is in B/C/S. Take it in your hands, please. Page 12. Do you see Article 35?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I have an English copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We should go through the document step-by-step, but this is just by way of introduction. Page 12, Article 35. Would you please read the first paragraph of Article 35, speaking of the types of decisions which may be passed by Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In performing the task within its field of action, the Municipal Assembly and its organs shall make decisions, issue orders and instructions and adopt solutions, conclusions, resolutions and recommendations. The general enactments of the Assembly shall be published in the Official Gazette of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So among the documents that can be issued by the Municipal Assembly and in Prijedor municipality after the 22nd of May, this has been replaced by the Crisis Staff. One of the documents is also an order. I believe that this may have confused you when the Judges asked you about the orders issued by the people representing the Crisis Staff. And you, as a soldier, were probably thinking only about those orders which belonged to the army, which are an integral part of the army. Can you see from this article that an order can also be a political enactment if it was issued by the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor municipality or its bodies?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never contested or talked about whether a Municipal Assembly can issue an order, but as a soldier, as a medical officer, as a doctor, I am used to military orders from the superior command, to reports from the subordinate command units, and according to the military regulations and the law on army and other military documents and based on what I adopted throughout my profession and education, I do not know any military documents or regulations that would say that anybody could issue orders to the army. And if, throughout the war, what I saw here, what I had read here had happened, to my mind these are just collateral events which were initiated by the Crisis Staffs, municipal organs, and reactions to that and what I could conclude based on the documents presented to me before this honourable Tribunal. So the reactions came from the assistance for moral education, and the reactions were what they were. So this is my line of thinking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is exactly what you said yesterday, but once again, let me ask you: Would there have been any consequences involving a member of the army if they had not followed such an order? In other words, would a military prosecutor have initiated proceedings against somebody who did not act in keeping with this political enactment called an order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody in the military command, none of its members, could suffer any consequences. And if they had suffered consequences, they would have been protected before the military court or by the military prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor. For the time being, let's put this document aside. We will need it later on. And now I would kindly ask the usher to show you the document number S346. First of all, the first sentence of the text, can you see who ordered the mobilisation? Was it ordered by a municipal organ or by a different organ?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the general mobilisation began.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked today, based on this same document, about the work obligation, the general work obligation. As an active military officer, you were a member of the army and, as such, you were not on any sort of work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even if you were, in fact, working as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just under the words "I hereby order" in the text, under number 1. We spoke about this yesterday, and we read the first article, which reads: "Immediately establish direct contact with municipal and military and territorial organs on the ground, offering expert and materiel support for the mobilisation process." The mobilisation process, does the Municipal Assembly take any part in this mobilisation process at all or is the Secretariat for National Defence totally in charge of that, which I mean is a department of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for National Defence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A municipal body?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretariat is part of the defence -- the Defence Ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a vertical line from the republic level down to the municipal level; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We spoke yesterday about Article 8 in this document, page 2. Item 4 reads -- I will do as Judge Vassylenko asked of you; I'll just read the first sentence out. Paragraph 8, and then item 4: "Until the units receive concrete combat tasks, engage them in the following tasks..." And then item 4: "Establish the closest possible cooperation with the people and legal authorities within their zones of responsibility." Does this specify what cooperation exactly is meant or is this just a very general piece of phrasing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible to live in a specific environment and not be surrounded by people who are part of that environment. I'm sitting here now. I'm looking at all of you here in the courtroom, and I communicate with you. So the military command must -- must speak up when it comes to a certain environment and must start communicating with its environment. So that's, I think, what is meant by this particular aspect of cooperation. But I was not under the impression that cooperation here meant deciding or making military decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell from this whether any kind of subordination or hierarchy was established, or was there an absence of subordination in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "subordination" is only familiar to me from the military environment. Outside the military, I'm not familiar with such forms of organisation or behaviour that could be called subordination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the next article, Article 9, and I'll read through Articles 10 and 11 too, these articles do refer to subordination, the concept of subordination. So I would just like to ask you whether this refers to military subordination of military units only. Item 9: "Strict military discipline, subordination, soldierly conduct, and constant vigilance and safety should be introduced from the very beginning in all units and commands."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is in the military sense, and this only applies to soldiers, to their commands, to the superiors or subordinates of a certain command, down to the common foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In -- as far as provisions are concerned, Article 10 reads: "Provision wartime units following the standard procedure and strictly prohibit any looting or other criminal acts on the ground." Therefore, even supplies were done according to an established scheme.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this refer to your military scheme of supply?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our own logistics base for military units, and every unit would express its needs. There'd be -- an assessment of their needs would be drawn up and it would be sent back to the base, and then the base would send whatever the units had requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 11: "Do not allow the presence of any paramilitary formations or other special organisations within the zones of responsibility. Disperse individual members among various units as volunteers, but if they refuse that, break them up, and if necessary, destroy them." Does this show that the army wants armed force only within their own units and that the army does not want to cooperate with some civilians who just happen to be walking about armed?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the army, you have no such concept as paramilitary units. Paramilitary units are considered an enemy unit, an enemy formation. They're not part of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 12 on page 3 reads: "Constantly monitor the progress of mobilisation and include the number of conscripts who have arrived and manning levels in percentages of wartime units at the battalion, regiment, and brigade level as a separate item in the regular combat report for the corps command." Do you see any reference here to the mobilisation and the course of mobilisation being reported to the Municipal Assembly or any of its bodies?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article here and what exactly is ordered in it, that's what had to be respected, that's what had to be complied with, and that's how you had to act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not be needing this document for the time being. May the usher now please show you document number S250.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please turn to page 6, document group number 9, item 2. You were asked yesterday about item 2, about conclusion number 02-111-171/92, assigning the duty of providing security for the Trnopolje camp to the regional command. Again, it is because of your military experience that we are using you here as an expert on constitutional law. However, to the best your knowledge, is this a political decision or can it also have the form of a military order if what is referred to herein is a military formation described as regional command?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has said time and time again that he's a medical doctor. He's not a lawyer and he's not a constitutional law expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You asked him the same questions, so I would follow. I'm following the questions of the Prosecution exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What we are doing at the moment is the following: You had the examination-in-chief. You brought us to the entire hierarchy down from the president of the republic to troops. And during the cross-examination, you were confronted with some documents from the perspective of the Prosecution tending to challenge that what has been said in the morning on the basis of concrete documents and based on documents in part - for example, the last one - addressed to the witness before us. Therefore, you can't say the witness is in a certain way abused as a lawyer or an expert in constitutional law. No. He was asked questions on the mere basis that he was a member of the military, no doubt in the area of health care and, therefore, it's a special situation, but I don't think that anybody has asked, besides the question whether or not the president was the one declaring war, that there were any other really legal questions. And therefore, already before I wanted to ask you to refrain as some months ago, when we started the same experiment, to refrain from asking questions the witness apparently can't answer. If it's limited to his own knowledge or based on his own career in the military, then the question is admissible, but not these questions in general. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to restrain to those questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pusac, I will try to ask a more specific question now. If you had received a conclusion of the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor municipality or the Banja Luka municipality, would you have treated that as an order on which you had to act?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, but I would have told my superior about it, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 8 of this document group number 13, you were asked yesterday about the order pursuant to which the Intervention Platoon was established. That's page 92, line 9, of yesterday's transcript. Do you have any information as to whether this Intervention Platoon or intervention squad was actually ever established?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So much for this particular document. The next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the usher please show the witness document S79.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is actually about the same Intervention Platoon, but as you seem to never have heard about this Intervention Platoon being set up at all, then I will refrain from asking you questions about this. The next document is D3, the statute of Prijedor municipality. On page 3, top of the page, Roman III, you see the rights and duties of the municipality. Article 7 reads: "In conformity with the constitution, the law and this statute, the municipality shall..." and if you would please turn the page. The next page, number 4, under item 5. Item 5 reads as follows: "Take appropriate measures for the protection of people and property, uphold law and order." Item 6: "Regulate and organise national defence, facilitate the realisation of the rights and duties of citizens in connection with the defence of the country, manage Territorial Defence and civil protection." I would just like to ask you the following -- excuse me. We'll leave this for later when we're dealing with S180, in order not to get things mixed up right now and to shift from one subject to another. So if the usher would please excuse me and show the witness document number S391. This document is referred to in the transcript on page 71, line 6. These are political conclusions from a subregional meeting of the municipalities of Bihac, Bosanski Petrovac, Srpska Krupa, Sanski Most, Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, and Kljuc. The Prosecution has tried to use this document, or more specifically item 4 of this document, to demonstrate that political organisations had the actual influence on the army. Item 1 of this document, on page 1, reads: "It is necessary to declare a state of war in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and this is requested on the 7th of June, 1992. Doctor, please tell us if you know whether a state of war was declared and when exactly.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was only towards the end of the war, in 1995, but certainly not before that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the army did not follow the instructions received from this political meeting, and the army did not declare a state of war in June 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to refer you now to the following: On page 2 of the same document, bottom of the page, next to the stamp. Can you see a signature or a name?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May the usher please show you document number S59. This is an excerpt from instructions for the work of the municipal Crisis Staff of the Serbian people. Can you please read out loud item 4.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The command of the TO and police forces is under the exclusive authority of the professional staff. Therefore, any interference regarding the command of the TO and/or the use of the police forces must be prevented."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document never refers to commanding the army.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think it's because the army is more difficult or easier to command than the police forces and the TO? Is there a possibility that civilian bodies of government, civilian authorities, interfered with the army and its commands? I'm talking about the municipal level now, because this document refers to Crisis Staffs at municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only professional persons, military professionals, can issue commands to the army, which means that the civilian authorities never had such people working there. They didn't have qualified military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. The next document I would like to show you is S4 -- 141. We'll use this document in connection with document S180. So if the usher could please place the Official Gazette of Prijedor municipality in front of you, the number is dated 25th of June, 1992. 2/92. I would like to follow the line of questioning by the Honourable Judge Schomburg, the same one he applied when referring to this document and asking you questions about it. So could you please now turn to page 76. The pages have the same numbers in both versions of the text, the original and the English translation. So please turn to page 76. Item 115. In the transcript, reference is being made to this document on page 87, from line 19 onwards. In your opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please wait one minute until we have the document before us. It's not yet on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 76 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think the English translation goes up to page 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's Exhibit number S180, and it has the same pagination as the B/C/S version. So page 76, item 115.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By this conclusion, the Crisis Staff suggests to the Prijedor regional command that it agree and rule on unified insignia for the army of Republika Srpska. I will remind you of the fact that the Assembly can pass decisions, orders, conclusions, resolutions, and recommendations. Is this an enactment that was passed by the Municipal Assembly or the Crisis Staff, the body that replaced it? Is that an order or is this a political enactment?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a recommendation, and it is a result of a political enactment, the political will and desire of this particular institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any military institution that had to obey this conclusion and act on it, according to your best knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no single command that could act without the approval of its superior command, and this, if this was to be an order to the military, this should have been passed by the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like you to go to page 35, which is page 2 of this document. Can you please look at Article 6. And the reference to that is made in transcript on page 89, from line 7 onwards. We have seen that the statute of Prijedor municipality, in its chapter number 3 on the rights and obligations of the municipality, in its Article 7 it prescribes that, in accordance with the statute law and this statute, the municipality, under item 6, it reads: "That the municipality will be in charge of organising the Territorial Defence, and it will secure the exercise of rights and duties of all citizens in connection with the defence of the state." In this Article 6, is there anything that is not in agreement with Article 7, item 6 of the statute of Prijedor municipality? In Article 6, therefore, are there just some more details provided as to the prescribed rights of the municipality to secure the exercise of the rights and obligations of citizens in connection with the defence of the state?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see anywhere in Article 6 that the Crisis Staff has the right to issue orders to the army? Can you please read Article 6 and tell us, please, whether you see anywhere that the Crisis Staff is in the position to issue any orders to the military.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Are you talking about page 35 of the Official Gazette, Article 6? "In the exercise of its function within the area of defence activities, the Crisis Staff shall, in particular, coordinate the work and activities of all components of All People's Defence, consider issues of mobilisation, development and reinforcement of the armed forces and other organisations, and foster their cooperation with other responsible municipal organs. On special request of the commander of the municipal Territorial Defence staff, deal with issues of supply requirements and funding sources for the Territorial Defence, keep abreast of all aspects of the situation in the municipality essential for the waging of armed combat and take appropriate measures, monitor the implementation of the recruitment planned and, where necessary, take measures for successful implementation thereof."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this Article 6, do you see anywhere the command role of the Crisis Staff with regard to the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday and again today, I persist in saying that the command of the army could not be and it wasn't regulated by the law on the army and other regulations regulating the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's now stay on the same page, but let's move to Article 9, which is referred to in transcript on page 90, line 1 and onwards. Article 9 reads: "The Crisis Staff shall at all times cooperate with the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Civil Defence, and public security through the senior officers or organs of these institutions. The Crisis Staff shall cooperate with all other business and public organisations in the municipality through the municipal Executive Committee." Can you see also here that this has to do with the exercise of rights and duties of citizens in connection with defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This transpires from this article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next thing that was discussed in this document is on page 37, item 20. This was referred to yesterday in the transcript on page 90, line 18. Here, from this order issued by the Municipal Assembly and the Crisis Staff which replaces it - and it has the right to do so based on Article 35 of the statute of the Municipal Assembly - this forbids unauthorised gunfire in the territory of the municipality of Prijedor. Doctor, the statute -- can you please pay attention? The statute, as we have read, of the municipality of Prijedor, in chapter III where it reads about the rights and obligations of the municipality, in Article 7, it reads: "In keeping with the constitution, law, and this statute of the municipality..." under item 5, it says: "Certain measures shall be taken in order to protect the people and their property aligned to. It is provided for public law and order." My question is: Is gunfire, unauthorised gunfire, considered disruption of public law and order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because this obviously -- it puts the people and property in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that this order was issued in keeping with the statute of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, Article 7, item 5? I have just read that part from the statute of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the statute as I have just read it to you, did the Municipal Assembly and the body that replaces it, the Crisis Staff, has the right to issue orders according to Article 35 of this statute?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but when it comes to the military and the military police, I as a soldier, and I believe that they understood this and the command as a form of an explanation as to what they were supposed to do with this regard, because the military police will react in cases when a soldier wearing a uniform will do something that goes against law and order, and the civilian police will react in the cases of civilians being involved. So I do not again think that this has anything to do with the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does civilian police have the right to arrest a soldier who is shooting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The civilian police can keep him, register him, and urgently call the military police for the military police to carry out investigation and undertake all the necessary measures against the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 42, yesterday you were asked about item 30. Again, this is yet another order. Under item 2, which is referred to in the transcript on page 91, line 13 and onwards, this order duty binds the commander of the Prijedor garrison and the public security station to establish the needs to engage materiel and technical equipment and deliver them to the municipal Secretariat for National Defence, so that the hitherto taken materiel and technical equipment may be given legitimacy. That is, the materiel and technical equipment that have been taken by the military and the police. Does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One moment, please. Could the usher please place item 30 on the ELMO. 3-0. Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's just discuss this item and then the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this order call upon the military and the police only to give a written document for something that they have already taken away or requisitioned, whatever you want to call that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the way I understand this order. I don't know of any other way I could understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is exactly what I have understood. And if the Honourable Judges think that this calls for further discussion, they can ask you questions on this later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Let's continue with our journey through the Official Gazette of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 51, item 48, you don't know anything about the Intervention Platoon, so I'm not going to ask you anything about it, but immediately move on to page 54, item 55, by which the Crisis Staff issued a decision relieving of his duties the commander of the Serbian Territorial Defence of Prijedor, Major Slobodan Kuruzovic. In connection with this item, I would like to ask the usher to give you document S141, and turn to page 44. In the English version, this is on page 59. Dr. Pusac, can you please read the title of the document on the first page. Can you please put the Official Gazette on the table. We will need the title page and page 44.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the minutes of the 16th session of the Assembly of the Serbian People held on the 12th of May? The session started --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I just needed the title. Let's now move to page 44. In the English version, this is on page 59, the last paragraph. In the B/C/S version, it is the beginning of the page. Can you please read the first paragraph on this page in this document.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Momcilo Krajisnik: We still have to adopt these amendments. Who is in favour? Who is against? Abstaining? So the amendments to the constitution have been adopted. Proceed, please. "Participant in the discussion: At the session held on 12 May, 1992 it adopted the law on the amendments to the National Defence Act, Article 1: In the National Defence Act, Official Gazette number 4/92, in all provisions of the act, the terms 'Territorial Defence' and 'armed forces' shall be replaced by the following words: 'The Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army.' "Article 2, subsection 2 of Article 10 is hereby expunged. It is an article in a subsection which regulated something concerning Territorial Defence. Article 3. Articles 37 to 53 also all have to do with Territorial Defence and are hereby expunged. Article 4. This act shall enter into effect eight days from its publication in the Official Gazette of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it transpire from this that already on the 12th of May, 1992, the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I'm clear that this really happened, and I couldn't know that before. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course we did not expect you to remember the date. When we go back to the Official Gazette number 2/92, page 54, item 55. I believe you have it open in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of the decision referred to within this Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 29 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 17 days after the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina disbanded or abolished the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the statute of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor in its Article 7, item 6, reads the following: "That the command over the Territorial Defence and Civilian Protection in the municipality," do you believe that the Crisis Staff, which at the time replaced the Municipal Assembly, actually only informed the former commander of Territorial Defence - of the former Territorial Defence - that he is hereby relieved of his duties because the formation whose member he was, that is whose commander he used to be, and which used to be under the command of the municipality, is only informed of the fact that his formation and his position had stopped existing 17 days before that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That formation indeed ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. We're approaching the end of our examination. Please bear with me for just a little longer. The honourable President Schomburg asked you about two further documents. One of them is on page 70 of the Official Gazette, Article 101, which was discussed on page 94 of yesterday's transcript, line 10 and onwards. In this conclusion, item 2: "The Autonomous Region of Krajina is requested to accelerate the establishment of an AP Autonomous Region of Krajina government as well as to clarify the conclusions of the Crisis Staff concerning the retirement of employees with 30 or 35 years of service." This conclusion, does it show any kind of discrimination with respect to retirees, against the retirees, or does it only refer to people who have simply served for 30 or 35 years, regardless of their ethnic background, which provides legal basis for an individual to retire?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any form of discrimination in this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document is on page 69. That's the page before this one. Article 97, near the top of the page. This conclusion was discussed during the hearing yesterday, page 95 of the transcript, line 10. If we read through this, its conclusion: "Because of the formation of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the need for the Serbian TO has ceased. The Serbian TO shall be incorporated into the structure of the region." This conclusion was also adopted on the 29th of May, 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document show that this conclusion was adopted because on the 20 -- on the 12th of May, 1992, the TO of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this conclusion establish the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This conclusion only informs that the army of Republika Srpska has been established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By this conclusion, is the TO of the Bosnian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina abolished?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This only informs that the TO had been abolished. That's probably why during the war I was not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your patience, Doctor. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm sure the Prosecution has some additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just three brief matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please. May, in the meantime, it please be taken care that the next witness arrives in due time. Thank you. Further cross-examined by Ms. Sutherland:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Pusac, you mentioned yesterday that you were in Banja Luka during the period April to September 1992 and that you weren't in Prijedor, and you said that the person in your position in Prijedor was Dr. Zeljko Macura; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to quote the page number of yesterday's transcript It facilitates the work.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise. In the LiveNote that I have in front of me, it's page 84, but I note that there was some text missing at the beginning of when I printed it out, so I think it's around page 84. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Pusac, you mentioned yesterday that you knew Dr. Zeljko Macura, who was a doctor. You stated that he was chief of the medical corps in the Prijedor garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend said that it's from -- that she forgot it yesterday or -- does it derive from my questions, my last questions or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was in relation to questions by the Judge, Judge Schomburg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I recall it. That's not the problem. But only to facilitate, to find it later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked by Judge Schomburg whom would you regard as your colleague or subordinate on the level of Prijedor responsible for taking care of all the health problems of this garrison command, and you said, your answer: "It was Dr. Macura. I cooperated with him and he was in that unit."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that I was permanently placed with my command and my service in Banja Luka. My command and my own service was not in Prijedor, and I never said that during my absence Dr. Macura was standing in for me, as you have just stated. I only said that I know Dr. Macura. He was the head of the medical unit in one of the Prijedor units. And when I was asked whether he had sent me any reports, I said clearly that he wasn't -- he wasn't duty-bound to send reports to me officially. His reports on medical activities were sent to the head of the medical corps, and the head of the medical corps at corps level was Dr. Branko Dikic. If memory serves me right, that's exactly what I stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. My question was: You were in Banja Luka. The person that was on your level in Prijedor was Dr. Macura; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Dr. Macura was at a lower level. He was at brigade level and I was in the medical battalion, directly subordinated to the corps command. I was at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Dr. Macura, you mentioned that he was -- was he an active-duty officer in 1992? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not an active-duty officer. He was a reserve duty officer, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he held any civilian or political positions in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to know show you a short video clip. Could you tell me whether you recognise anyone in this video.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the video please be played. And this is Exhibit S7.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Without the sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you recognise anyone, could you please ask for the video to be paused.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is Dr. Kovacevic, the man in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the white shirt, with a cigarette in his hand?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a moustache. I knew the man.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Please play --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And -- no. I'm not positive. This person reminds me of Zeljaja, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which person are you pointing to? And the time clock, for the record, is 11.37.01.01.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one with the head bowed. Yes, this man with his head down. This man looks like Zeljaja, but I can't be sure. From this angle, I really can't tell for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the man with the head --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man here, with his hand over his face, wearing uniform, he looks like him, but I'm not sure from this angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person that you said you thought was Zeljaja, you said he had his head bowed. Is that the one towards the back of the still, in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour is his hair?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The image is flickering, so it's very difficult for me to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just stop the video, and can you rewind the video a moment. Stop. Can you play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone else in this video?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise these people wearing uniforms. I don't know any of them. Will you please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise Dr. Macura in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, now that you've had the tape rewound, I think I did notice him, Dr. Macura.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where he's sitting on the table. Ask for the videotape to be paused when you have identified him.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not here. Can you just rewind a little bit, please? Here. I think he's scratching his head or going with his fingers through his hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man looks a bit like Macura, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is stopped at 11.37.00.20, and it's the man in the very front of the still, on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the video be played.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Stop. Could the video just be rewound -- stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that Dr. Macura on --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, left-hand side, right-hand side from --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the still, is that Dr. Macura? Where is Dr. Macura sitting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is wearing uniform. There are three persons here in this frame, and Dr. Macura is wearing uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I do have a problem with my left and my right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that frame is at 11.37.07.03?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the transcript, it's not contested that we speak about the person at the right-hand side from our point of view, and the only one in uniform here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. The video can be stopped now. Could the witness be shown Exhibit S180, which is the Prijedor Official Gazette, number 2 of 92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, could you please turn to page 35 and look at item number 19.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 35.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item number 19, which is the decision on the appointments to the Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 35, I don't have Article 19. I have Article 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you go to page 36, and it goes over onto page 37.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-six. Yes, I can see Article 19 on page 36.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it states there, does it not, that Dr. Macura was appointed to the Prijedor Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Which article are we discussing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article number 19.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decision on appointments to Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And look at appointment number 10.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- and that's the Dr. Macura that you have referred to in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I would just like the witness to clarify in which capacity Dr. Macura was a member of the Crisis Staff in the municipality of Prijedor. So just read point 10 entirely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As we did it previously, could you please be so kind, on the request of the Defence, read out point 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Article 19: Pursuant to Article 110 of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Official Gazette of the Serbian people --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's not necessary, only --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doctor, excuse my interruption, but the next page, page 37. Could you please turn to page 37, number 10, referring to Dr. Macura. Just read that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Dr. Zeljko Macura, health and social security officer, secretary, at Prijedor municipal Secretariat for Economy and Social Affairs, appointed to the post of member."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this appointment -- does this post have anything to do with the army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. You have the right to come back to this question in a moment. It's for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you was did Dr. Macura hold any political or civilian positions in 1992 and I think you said that you weren't aware and I have taken you to this document which shows that he did hold a civilian or political position in 1992, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have such information, and on the basis of this perhaps you do. I said I didn't myself. Throughout the war, I didn't know whether he was involved in politics or a member of any political body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the same time that he was appointed to be a member of the Prijedor Crisis Staff, he was also a reserve officer in the military. Isn't that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reserve officer, but whether at the same time, I mean his mobilisation and his involvement in political activities, whether these were actually simultaneous or parallel, I don't know. And secondly, he was not an active-duty officer. He came from civilian life. He was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. I'll move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit D51.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, this morning you were shown an exhibit by Mr. Lukic, S391, and you stated that the army didn't follow the instructions received from the political meeting of the subregion of the different municipalities that had a meeting on the 7th of June, 1992. Could you please go to page 3 in the document in your language, paragraph 6. And we note that D51 is a document dated the 13th of June, 1992. Does it not say halfway down paragraph 6: "The purging of officers on an ethnic basis remains a topic of discussion because of the danger that it may very soon result in deficiencies in the units, but it is proceeding in the spirit of the order received"? Do you see the sentence that I just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is -- this is a regular combat report sent from General Talic to the Main Staff, is it not, D51?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, within the command there is always an officer for morale, and that's the sort of activity that that body was pursuing, and they would discuss requests of this nature which reached the command. But this was forwarded to a higher command level, and then an order would be sent down from the top level, but certainly not from municipal Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We discussed yesterday Exhibit S391, which was the meeting of the subregions of the municipalities on the 7th of June, and they sent a request to the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region Krajina and the Serbian government, requesting them to purge Muslim and Croat officers from the corps. Then we had Exhibit S392, which was dated the 9th of June, 1992, which discussed the Crisis Staff decision of the 8th of June and talked about 67 officers of Muslim and Croat ethnicity being dismissed from the corps. And then we had -- that was signed by Vukelic from the 1st Krajina Corps, asking for assistance. That was a document being sent to the Main Staff, asking for guidance in relation to this specific issue. And then I showed you Exhibit 393, which was the document dated the same day, the 9th of June, signed by Ratko Mladic, saying dismiss all Muslims and Croats, immediately put them on leave. Now, this document here is dated four days after General Mladic's order, and the sentence that I just read to you: "The purging of officers on an ethnic basis remains a topic of discussion because of the danger that it may very soon result in deficiencies in the units, but it is proceeding in the spirit of the order received." And that is the order sent by General Mladic not four days previously.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yesterday I did comment on that order by General Mladic. And if I may add, I personally know officers of Muslim ethnicity who were probably sent into retirement on the basis of that order. They lived throughout the war in Banja Luka. A neighbour of mine who was a friend of mine who lived in the same building as I did, throughout the war, both his wife and he were Muslims, but he is still there. Now the question is: Was that a crime being committed against him? Was it a crime? I'll leave it up to the Honourable Court to decide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. The final topic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit S61.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were taken this morning to Exhibit S346, which was the document dated the 21st of May, 1992, signed by Momir Talic dealing with mobilisation, and you were asked if there was any reference in the document to the mobilisation and the course of mobilisation being reported to the Municipal Assembly or any of its bodies, and you replied that there wasn't. Could I ask you to look at Exhibit S61, which is a decision on the mobilisation on the territory of Prijedor municipality dated the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document, and what should be done, they probably know pursuant to the statute and to the constitution. I'm not familiar with that. And what their duties were, to inform the municipality. But what I said, pursuant to the order by General Talic in which he informs that the Presidency of the republic had proclaimed general mobilisation, and in that sense, that military units should send reports to their superior military commands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document S61 states: "Pursuant to the decision of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the general public mobilisation of forces and materiel in the Republic, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality, considering the current situation and conditions, at the meeting held on the 22nd of May, 1992, reached a decision on the mobilisation on the territory of Prijedor municipality." My question to you, Doctor, is this: Based on your knowledge of Dr. Stakic, of who Dr. Stakic was, was he the type of person to issue orders without any authority?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knowing Dr. Stakic as a person, as a colleague and as a citizen, I believe that he never wanted to -- that he would never have ordered anything that he was not authorised to order, or order anything that he could be held liable for. That's my firm belief, and that's my opinion of Dr. Stakic. Personally, I didn't have any such information, and I didn't have any documents that would point to that. I am not a lawyer, but I told you what I think and what I firmly believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I had the impression that the Defence had a question in return.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a few, Your Honour. Thank you. Further re-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pusac, the position held by Dr. Zeljko Macura, and I'm going to read his title, that is, the officer for health care and social protection in the municipal Secretariat for Economy and Social Affairs. So is that position in any way connected with the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. It is a position within the health care, and it is a duty that a doctor can perform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we say in our midst that somebody is an officer, is that a political function?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An officer. That is a professional duty for which somebody is paid and receives salary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is not considered as a functionary? Somebody who is an officer does not need to have a function?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. It is a job. It is a job title.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding the last question that the Prosecution put to the witness, we would like to show this document to the witness. It has here a number, but we don't have an exhibit number nor do we have a translation. Please show it to the witness. It could be put on the ELMO. We don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could we please --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the Defence read the ERN number so that we could possibly check the computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 00574584 and 85. I would not be surprised that this is already admitted into evidence. May it be shown to the Prosecution and then put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. It's Exhibit S21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I saw it before. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could the lower part of the document be shown, please. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 11018 to 11022. "Decision" and -- we need actually "Decision" part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pusac, at the bottom of this page, we can see the last part of the decision, but firstly we are interested in the body that issued this document, and when was that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of Defence in Sarajevo, date 16 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now at the bottom of the page, we can see: "Pursuant to Article 81 of the statute of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and on the proposal of the government, the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina hereby issues the following..." and can you please read the rest.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lower part you mean? Number 1: "A state of an imminent threat of war is here by declared. "2. It is hereby ordered that general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence should take place in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. All military conscripts are duty-bound to make themselves available to the municipal Territorial Defence staffs in the territory of the Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was at a time when the Territorial Defence still existed?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered the general mobilisation referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina. In other words, the Ministry of Defence, that is. The Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the ministry received from the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was held on the 15th of April. That was an Assembly of the -- and pursuant to that article, the ministry issued a decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this in keeping with your allegations that nobody at the level of the municipality cannot call for the general public mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That is obvious. I'm not that familiar with all these matters, but all the military conscripts, I believe, know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Pusac. I have no further questions to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other questions? I can see no questions. Dr. Pusac, I have to thank you for this mutual cooperation in criminal matters; mutual because apparently it was not only that all the participants put questions to you, but at the same time you were confronted with documents you hadn't seen before, and as you stated previously, it will be for the Trial Chamber to evaluate the probative value of these documents, and your testimony was, no doubt, of assistance in this procedure. Thank you for coming to The Hague, and I wish you a safe trip home to your country and to your home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. You're excused for today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Everybody has the right of freedom to move wherever he wants, so -- In the meantime, I took the liberty to extend our apologies to the next witness that, once again, she has to wait until half past one. So we can't begin now. But let us take the opportunity. We are seized with the Defence motion for disclosure of exculpatory material, per Rule 68 of 22 January 2003. This was as an exception to our Rules, on the request of the OTP that we receive this in writing. May I ask the OTP, do they agree and do they accept this request or do you believe it's necessary that the Trial Chamber explicitly hands down an order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the OTP plans to file a written response. It's another team that's actually handling it. They just received the motion last night, and I haven't discussed in detail their position, but they will respond in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have to postpone the decision, but please, let's have the answer, if possible, no later than tomorrow, because it might be that the witness involved appears earlier than expected and we have to be prepared, and no doubt the Defence has the right to prepare the testimony of this witness. Any other urgent - emphasise "urgent" - matters to be discussed right now? I can see none. Then it's exactly high noon, and the trial stays adjourned until half past one. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.00 noon 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. I anticipate there is a request by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in response to the issue raised at the end of the morning's session, I was in contact with the team that's handling the Krajisnik case and formerly the Plavsic and Krajisnik case - I guess still technically that case - and they are requesting to have 14 days to respond to the motion, as provided for in the Rules under normal circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the submission by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
