I didn't move about a lot, and my circumstances in the family were such that I waited for the working day to be over, for me to go home. I didn't talk about it, and maybe you could take these circumstances into consideration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: On any occasion did you see Dr. Stakic leaving the office or see him outside the office, whether from your desk or when you were in the corridor or when you were going to lunch or leaving work, in the presence of other individuals?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I could see him in the corridor, nowhere else, with other people working in the administrative bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other people would you see Dr. Stakic with?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. May I have a time frame at least to know what period counsel is referring to and perhaps even a year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, what other individuals did you see Dr. Stakic with?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me about the times when he left his office, in that sense, but that is only when he opens the door and comes across somebody in front of his door, because I didn't follow him anywhere outside his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, madam, let me understand how well you know Dr. Stakic. On your examination earlier, you indicated, am I correct, that you have a very good understanding of the character of Dr. Stakic? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I understand you, you sat at your desk outside his office, you didn't listen to any of the conversations that took place inside his office, you never saw him out of work and only saw him passing by; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. When he was passing by, there were people waiting for him, clients, he was very polite to them. Or when somebody asked for him, he would receive them. And all of that said to me that he was a kind and polite person who communicated nicely with people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when Radoslav Brdjanin came to Prijedor in 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to remind you. Do you remember when Stojan Zupljanin and Radoslav Brdjanin came to Prijedor in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I say yes, because you didn't mention Zupljanin at first. You just said Brdjanin. That's why I said no. And yes, Zupljanin did come in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection after the answer. Can counsel show the witness that Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Zupljanin came together to Prijedor? Because until now, we didn't know for the fact that they were together on that day. And other witnesses testified that it was only Zupljanin, just Zupljanin, not Brdjanin. That's what we know. Perhaps I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I can respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please take this into account, and I would immediately have some answer, but it's not for me to react now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who Radoslav Brdjanin was?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he lived in Banja Luka and -- no. I can't be sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic receive Mr. Zupljanin in his office on that occasion in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: They were not in the office. The meeting, I was told, was in the big conference room. So it's not in the part where we worked. You had to go, take a different way to get there. So I didn't know who was at the meeting, but in any case, Zupljanin did not come to Stakic's office or anybody else at the time, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't it part of your duties to help prepare for a visit like that, such as calling other individuals to appear, to receive Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, did you -- was it part of your duties to prepare for the visit of foreign journalists to Prijedor in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you arrange for the interpreter to come -- an interpreter to come to the Municipal Assembly building in August of 1992 when Penny Marshall, Ed Vulliamy, and another foreign journalist came to Prijedor and visited the Omarska and Trnopolje camps?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't call a meeting, but the lady who interpreted, I called her subsequently because somebody came from the big conference room and told me Mr. Drljaca asked for Nada to be here to interpret from English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else did you call to come to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody else. It was not my duty to call anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you know, whose duty was it to arrange for meetings of Dr. Stakic to call other individuals who were invited to meetings with Dr. Stakic in the Municipal Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: It was Zupljanin who arrived and it was nobody else but somebody from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zupljanin is from Banja Luka and Dr. Stakic was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you testified about Dr. Stakic's good relations and treatment of non-Serbs. Can you tell me now the names of any Muslims or Croats that were invited by Dr. Stakic to his office after June, from June 1st through the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims that Dr. Stakic called. Can you please repeat the question? I'm not sure I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic ask you to call any Muslims or Croats after June 1, 1992, to come meet with him?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about -- excuse me. You talked about the correct relationship between Professor Cehajic and Dr. Stakic and that from all of the interactions you observed they appeared to be on good terms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in January of 1992 the declaration of a -- this is before the takeover, but the declaration of a Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to remind you, because I realise it's been a long time ago and perhaps the question could confuse you for a moment. Is it -- do you recall now that the SDS party formed their own government before the takeover and Dr. Stakic was named the president but the government of -- this is before the takeover -- the government of Professor Cehajic continued to operate?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I've never heard of this before. This is the first time I hear about it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try just once more, because perhaps -- I know it's been a long time ago. Do you recall the declaration of a Serbian Assembly of Prijedor in which Dr. Stakic was appointed the president? Do you recall Professor Cehajic congratulating him on obtaining that position?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, would it -- I'm going to read a portion of S47A. It's a Kozarski Vjesnik article from the 28th of April 1994. Please don't concern yourself with the number. I'm giving the number so Mr. Lukic can follow, and the Judges. Excuse me; Mr. Ostojic. I don't want to forget him. In this article, ma'am, I'm quoting at the end of the third paragraph, it quotes Dr. Stakic, Milomir Stakic, as saying: "On direction of the central office of the SDS, we formed the Serbian Assembly of Prijedor and I became chairman. When I arrived to work the next day, the then chairman of the joint Assembly, Muhamed Cehajic, greeted me with the following words: 'Hello colleague. Now we are both chairmen, and I congratulate you from all my heart and wish you success.'" I'm not asking you if you remember that, but is what I just read, the quotation from Professor Cehajic, consistent with what you observed about how he treated Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is consistent. They worked together. They cooperated. If that really happened, whether it did or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The article goes on to quote Dr. Stakic as saying: "But in spite of his smile, I knew what was behind these words and what they are planning to do to us." Did Dr. Stakic ever express to you his belief that Professor Cehajic was being deceptive in acting friendly to him and really was planning on doing evil to the Serbian people of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Stakic never told me anything connected with non-Serbian population, and especially Cehajic, because this is the relationship we had, and the president did not have to share his opinions with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having worked directly with Professor Cehajic for almost a year and a half, were you concerned with his fate in 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was very sorry about his fate as a human being. Later on, I'd heard that he was gone, that he was no longer amongst us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992, out of these human feelings, did you ever ask Dr. Stakic about Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover of Prijedor and removal of Professor Cehajic from the position he was elected to, did Dr. Stakic ever talk about Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: About Professor Cehajic, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, when you went to work in the summer of 1992, would you see the SUP building on your way into or out of work?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see long lines of women standing outside of that building?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Women and also men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the ethnicity of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Muslim and Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that something that everyone who worked in the Municipal Assembly building would have been aware of, that there were long lines of women and others in front of the SUP building all during the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: That I really don't know. They could have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about the working day of Dr. Stakic in 1992? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just object to the form of the question. Is it during his time when he was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly or during the time he was president of the Municipal Assembly or both or neither?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, during the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When the Defence counsel insists on this policy, we will take the same measures in the future also based on the questions put to the witness by the Defence. So may I ask you to break down the question and split it up into certain periods of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover of the municipality of Prijedor until, let's say, the end of September 1992, so throughout the spring and summer of 1992 after the takeover, when Dr. Stakic took over the position and office of Professor Cehajic, can you tell us what his workday was like?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992. I'm trying to read this. This is a long question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the office of Professor Cehajic or the office of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're mentioning Cehajic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what's the point. Is there any other office outside the municipal building or it's the same office?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, do you know what office Professor Cehajic had before the takeover?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who took that office?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic took the office of the president of Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And madam, if you're ever confused with my question, please ask me and I'll clarify it, as I believe you've done on several occasions. Can you tell us what you know about the workday of Dr. Stakic from the 30th of April, 1992, through the end of September.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: What was his workday like. I'd see him when he came to the office. We'd greet each other. He'd go to his office. If needed, he would ask me to call someone, or if there was someone waiting for him already, then he would just usher the person into his office himself. The rest of the day, when there were phone calls to the president, that's when I'd go into the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: And the whole of the working day would -- should I continue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. We're interested in any information you can give us.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: The whole working day could be summed up in this communication by telephone. Of course this very much depended on whether there were any callers who were already there or some who came later or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time normally Dr. Stakic would arrive at and leave the office?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: As Dr. Stakic travelled, you can say that he was never late for work. Maybe a minute or two, as far as I remember, because it didn't really matter to me. I wasn't really watching closely when Dr. Stakic would arrive to work, whether he was punctual or not. Someone might have detained him outside in the street, talking to him. So your question was when did he come to work? You could say he was punctual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us the hours? I'm not familiar what the normal working hours were when he would come and leave. Was it 7.00 a.m., 8.00 a.m.? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Our working hours were between 8.00 and 2.00, 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, you talked about -- let me ask you. Did Dr. Stakic have a driver?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Dr. Stakic would go? Would he tell you where he was going when he was out of the office?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he leave word with you as to when he would return?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He'd say, "I'll be back right away, in half an hour," that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Dr. Stakic travelling to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic call individuals in Banja Luka that you recall?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember phone calls to Mr. Brdjanin, for example?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prijedor municipality consists of a number of different villages, settlements, correct, and the big town.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic visit all of the areas or other areas of Prijedor besides the town?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Dr. Stakic live throughout 1992 - I was going from January until the end of 1992 - to the best of your knowledge? And if there is a distinction, if it changed after the takeover, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: When Dr. Stakic was the vice-president, he would travel from Omarska, and then for a while after the takeover, but I couldn't specify the period. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after he stopped travelling from Omarska? Do you know where he was living then?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: He lived in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In his automobile, did he have any means of communication, to your knowledge? Was there any type of radio or mobile telephone or -- or, like, police radio?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I never went into his car, but if I may say, I was never inside an official car during all of my time working for the municipality. I had my reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have phone numbers where you could reach Dr. Stakic when he was not in the office?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was only the private number at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic wear a gun?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you remember if you ever saw him wearing a gun?

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: I would remember, yes. He could have carried a gun in his bag without my seeing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic wear a uniform? Let me be more precise: Did he wear a camouflage uniform like a military-type uniform? Either camouflage or olive-grey. I'm sorry. I'm just trying to be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: STOJA RADAKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, he did, but only on festive occasions. For example, when fresh recruits were being sent off to the army, there'd be a festivity there and he'd wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just object to the interpretation, for the record, Your Honour. It's not accurate that it's festive occasion, it's more ceremonial, but we don't need to dispute that now; just so it's noted in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the booth the correct --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We agree with Mr. Ostojic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification, Mr. Ostojic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be a good time to break, if Your Honour wants to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial then stays adjourned until tomorrow, but before we take the break, I have to tell you, and I have to currently ask you not to contact any of the parties, be it the Prosecution or any member of the Defence team, or in case you may meet another witness here in The Hague, please do not discuss with anybody about that what you have testified today, and don't discuss the issues which may be relevant for your future testimony. Did you understand this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial then stands adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.
